events.title: UN General Assembly Adopts Partition Plan for Palestine
events.description: The United Nations General Assembly voted 33 to 13, with 10 abstentions, to adopt Resolution 181, which recommended partitioning British Mandate Palestine into independent Arab and Jewish states with Jerusalem under international administration.
events.significance: The resolution was accepted by Jewish leaders and rejected by Arab leaders. Civil war in Mandatory Palestine followed, and the 1948 Arab-Israeli War came after it, shaping the Israeli-Palestinian conflict to this day.

events.title: Warren Commission Established
events.description: President Lyndon B. Johnson created the President's Commission on the Assassination of President Kennedy, chaired by Chief Justice Earl Warren, to investigate the assassination of John F. Kennedy a week earlier.
events.significance: The commission concluded in 1964 that Lee Harvey Oswald acted alone. Its findings have been debated ever since and have fueled lasting public interest in conspiracy theories and later congressional investigations.

events.title: Atari Releases Pong
events.description: Atari, founded by Nolan Bushnell and Ted Dabney, installed its arcade game Pong, developed by engineer Allan Alcorn, at Andy Capp's Tavern in Sunnyvale, California.
events.significance: Pong became the first commercially successful arcade video game, launching the video game industry as a mass-market form of entertainment.

events.title: Founding of FC Barcelona
events.description: Swiss-born footballer Joan Gamper placed an advertisement seeking players, and on November 29 a group of players founded Futbol Club Barcelona in Barcelona, Spain.
events.significance: FC Barcelona grew into one of the world's most successful and popular football clubs, and has become a symbol of Catalan identity and a global sports and cultural institution.

events.title: Sand Creek Massacre
events.description: Colorado territorial militia led by Colonel John Chivington attacked a village of Cheyenne and Arapaho people at Sand Creek in southeastern Colorado Territory, killing at least 150 people, most of them women, children, and elderly.
events.significance: The massacre provoked widespread outrage and government investigations, intensified the Plains Indian Wars, and remains a defining example of violence against Native Americans during westward expansion.
